definitions.explanation: An undesirable situation or outcome that someone ends up in, typically as a result of their own actions or circumstances beyond their control. Almost always used in the pattern 〜する{羽目|はめ}になる.

examples.japanese: ⟦{電車|でんしゃ}→電車：00522_densha⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦{乗|の}り{遅|おく}れて→乗り遅れる：04621_noriokureru⟧、⟦{歩|ある}く→歩く：00538_aruku⟧{羽目|はめ}になった。
examples.english: I missed the train and ended up having to walk.

examples.japanese: ⟦{約束|やくそく}→約束：01517_yakusoku⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{忘|わす}れて→忘れる：00474_wasureru⟧、⟦{謝|あやま}る→謝る：01177_ayamaru⟧{羽目|はめ}になった。
examples.english: I forgot my promise and ended up having to apologize.

examples.japanese: ⟦{安|やす}い→安い：00464_yasui⟧⟦から→から：00504_kara⟧⟦と→と：00512_to⟧{飛|と}びついたら、⟦{修理|しゅうり}→修理：03214_shuuri⟧⟦{代|だい}→〜代：28331_dai⟧⟦で→で：00502_de⟧⟦{余計|よけい}→余計：04090_yokei⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦{払|はら}う→払う：00535_harau⟧{羽目|はめ}になった。
examples.english: I jumped at it because it was cheap, but ended up paying even more in repair costs.

notes:
USAGE:
{羽目|はめ} is almost exclusively used in the pattern 〜⟦する→する：00392_suru⟧{羽目|はめ}⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦なる→なる：01970_naru⟧ (to end up having to ~), expressing an undesirable outcome. It always carries a negative nuance — the speaker did not want this result.

KEY PATTERN:
- verb (dictionary form) + {羽目|はめ}⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦なる→なる：01970_naru⟧ (to end up having to ~)
- ⟦{払|はら}う→払う：00535_harau⟧{羽目|はめ}⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦なる→なる：01970_naru⟧ (to end up having to pay)
- ⟦{待|ま}つ→待つ：00469_matsu⟧{羽目|はめ}⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦なる→なる：01970_naru⟧ (to end up having to wait)
- ⟦やり{直|なお}す→やり直す：03172_yarinaosu⟧{羽目|はめ}⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦なる→なる：01970_naru⟧ (to end up having to redo it)

SIMILAR WORDS:
- 〜⟦する→する：00392_suru⟧{羽目|はめ}⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦なる→なる：01970_naru⟧: emphasizes the undesirable result
- 〜⟦する→する：00392_suru⟧はめ⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦なる→なる：01970_naru⟧: same meaning (sometimes written without kanji)
- 〜⟦ざる→ざる：04470_zaru⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{得|え}ない→得る：02014_eru⟧: "have no choice but to" (more formal, less focus on misfortune)
